$comment: Allowlist for check_earned_signal.py (CLAUDE.md §N.8 Earned-Signal Principle; SAMĀPTI v2.0 §7.5, lane B-N8-LINT). Same shape as fact_category_pin_allowlist.json (#840) with ONE addition: `max_occurrences`. An entry requires `file` (repo-relative POSIX, exact match) and `field` (the signal name, exact match), plus EITHER `line` (exact) OR `pattern` (regex, falling back to substring, against the snippet) OR neither — a file+field entry with neither is a deliberate group disposition, and MUST then carry `max_occurrences`, which freezes the group at its rollout size. Occurrence N+1 in a frozen group is reported as NEW and fails the build, so this backlog can be paid down but never grown. An entry with no `field` never matches anything (fails closed, not open). HONESTY NOTE, required by the lane's own charter: the entries below are CATEGORICAL dispositions from a sampled review, not 81 individual code reviews. Each says which category it is in and whether it was individually examined. `sample_lines`/`sample_snippet` are locators recorded at rollout, not match keys — they may drift and are not used for matching.

INDIVIDUALLY REVIEWED false positive, Paripraśna P1 lane G1-A. `assess_health` here is not a verdict/verified-status field — it is a KEY in `CAPABILITY_CLASS_RULES`, a static `Record<string, SafetyClass>` lookup table mapping MCP tool/capability names (assess_health is a real tool name) to the safety class that capability implies. It is structurally identical to its untouched neighbours in the same object literal (get_ayurdaya, ganita_ayurdaya_get, get_medical_indications, ...), none of which tripped the lint — only this key's name happens to match the health-related signal-name heuristic. No detector is needed because no verification claim is being made; this is configuration data, not a computed result. Adding a detector here would be inventing one for a claim the code never makes. Line corrected 997→1018 on 2026-08-20 (HS-4 death-anniversary false-positive fix, attempt 1, added comments earlier in the same file, shifting this line). Line corrected again 1018→1046 on 2026-08-20 (same-day attempt 2: an adversarial review of attempt 1 found a regression — narrowing the shared `MORTALITY_TERMS_A` lexicon broke downstream hard-stop combination rules — so attempt 1 was superseded by a corrected fix that reverts `MORTALITY_TERMS_A` and instead introduces a separate `MORTALITY_TERMS_A_STANDALONE_REVIEW` constant, adding further lines above this point in the same file. Same reviewed entry both times, no new review needed — this key's own content and neighbours are unchanged).

INDIVIDUALLY REVIEWED false positive, Paripraśna P2 lane P2-E (observability, PPR-33/GAP-14). `lintLeaksTotal` is a private mutable accumulator field on `TurnMetricsCollector`, initialized to 0 as its starting value — not a verdict/verified-status literal that never changes. It is incremented at line 99 (`this.lintLeaksTotal += leakCount`) inside `recordRegisterLint(leakCount: number)`, whose only caller (`synthesis_stage.ts`) passes the REAL `deltaLint.leakCount` returned by `lintReaderProse` on every streamed delta — a genuine program input, not a constant. The accumulated value is read back at line 126 into the `leaks_total` field of the snapshot persisted to `llm_usage_events`. The linter's static pattern-matcher flags the `= 0` initializer without seeing the later `+=` mutation from real input; the class's own docstring and its colocated tests (`turn_metrics.test.ts`) demonstrate the accumulation with real, varying leak counts. No detector is needed beyond the accumulation itself — the field IS the detector's running total, not a claim standing in for one.

INDIVIDUALLY REVIEWED false positive, Nirmana tracker campaign spine. These two entries are static lookup-table keys: one maps the fixed lifecycle milestone ID to the evidence event type and the other maps the same milestone ID to operator guidance. They are not emitted verification results. `projectAssetMilestones` determines the milestone state from accepted event records in the campaign definition cohort, so changing either literal cannot manufacture a verified asset. The key is allowlisted with a fixed occurrence ceiling so a new `verified` literal in this file still fails CI.

INDIVIDUALLY REVIEWED false positive, Paripraśna P2 lane G3-B (interpretation_sets, PPR-02). `domain_verdict` here is a KEY in `CATEGORY_PRIORITY`, a static `Readonly<Record<string, number>>` sort-priority lookup table (values 0-4) used only to order truncation when a turn has more significant judgments than `MAX_SIGNIFICANT_JUDGMENTS_PER_TURN` allows — structurally identical in kind to P1's `assess_health`/`CAPABILITY_CLASS_RULES` case already allowlisted above (same file-pattern: a signal-shaped key name in a static config object, not a verdict/verified-status field). No detector is needed because no verification claim is being made about `domain_verdict` itself; the actual detection of a domain-verdict judgment happens elsewhere (`interpretation/detect.ts`, keyed off the real `role === 'verdict'` block classification), and IS earned there. This table only decides truncation order among already-detected categories.

INDIVIDUALLY REVIEWED source-contract metadata, Purna Anvesana W7-P1. This is not a runtime success verdict: it declares that the additional aggregate binding's semantic collection lives at the reviewed `components` path. The target descriptor declares `components` as an array, the aggregate handler constructs it from all nine canonical scalar outcomes, and query_current_transit_snapshot.test.ts plus beyond_acarya_acceptance.test.ts exercise successful, partial, forged-identity and missing-anchor paths. The occurrence ceiling is one; any second literal in this file still fails the gate. Pagination is `none` and is deliberately recorded as null rather than a fabricated pass.
